howToRecordADecision: Replace NOT REVIEWED only with your own decision, name, role, the actual review date and the commit or content version you reviewed. A decision covers that item's scope: the accuracy and safety of the explanation and of any simulated consequence, not a learner and not the module. items.learnerWording: Transfer stem: “With an irregular rhythm, some assisted beats are mistimed. What is the most defensible way to evaluate a trigger change?” Best: “Select the most reliable trigger available and verify the timing on the trace”. Before this batch, “Keep ECG triggering…” was graded a wrong mechanism (“no source is universally superior”) and the optional exercise was satisfied only once the trigger was no longer ECG, including internal triggering.
items.intendedTeachingPoint: A trigger is judged by where inflation and deflation land on the arterial trace, beat by beat, in whatever rhythm the patient has.

sourceLocations.note: Pressure triggering is not recommended with sustained irregular rhythms or tachyarrhythmias. Do not remain in internal trigger mode when the patient is generating a cardiac output. The model rates pressure triggering best in atrial fibrillation and clears its trigger alarm.

sourceLocations.location: Printed p. 2-18 (PDF 104), 'Dysrhythmias while in pressure trigger'
sourceLocations.note: In pressure trigger the console detects atrial fibrillation and deflates earlier automatically; the user should not adjust deflation. The model represents no such console compensation.

sourceLocations.location: Printed p. 3 (PDF 5), ECG and pressure triggers
sourceLocations.note: ECG: preferred trigger with a reliable R wave; recommended for patients with arrhythmias. Pressure: backup trigger; not recommended for irregular rhythms such as atrial fibrillation.

Asynchronous, 80 bpm (40–120); typically on bypass with no QRS, or in CPR when compressions give too little pulse pressure. Do not remain in internal trigger when the patient is generating a cardiac output. The capstone opens on internal triggering in a patient with output.

Outside-US guide: internal trigger only when there is no mechanical cardiac cycle; ECG the trigger of choice with an adequate R wave; pressure the trigger of choice with a regular rhythm when the R wave is inadequate.

sourceCheck.result: The supplied Cardiosave material consistently prefers ECG triggering in arrhythmia, advises against pressure triggering in sustained irregular rhythm, and reserves internal triggering for the absence of a cardiac cycle. The model's atrial fibrillation coefficients rank these the other way round for ECG and pressure.
sourceCheck.notChecked: Other consoles; the Cardiosave B.17 material the device profile names; the current US IFU revision; the registered Getinge web page.

items.modelOutput: Atrial fibrillation transfer setup: ECG 50% synchrony with the trigger-unreliable alarm, effective 3.51, MAP 67; pressure 74%, no alarm, effective 3.60, MAP 69; internal 40% with the alarm, effective 3.48. Sinus reference: ECG 100%, pressure 90%, internal 62%. Coefficients in computeIabpSupport: atrial fibrillation pressure 0.74, ECG 0.5, internal 0.4. The IABP-02 signal (synchrony at least 60) and CAP-IABP-01 signal (at least 65) are reachable in this rhythm only with pressure triggering.

items.missingAndReassess: The model does not represent R-wave quality, a console's automatic handling of an irregular rhythm, or asynchronous internal inflation against native beats. What to check: the R wave, the console's own instructions and irregular-rhythm handling, and inflation and deflation landmarks beat by beat on the arterial trace.

items.topic: First response to a suction pattern at high support

learnerSurfaces.locator: Suction transfer stem
learnerSurfaces.excerpt: At high support, preload falls and a suction pattern appears with lower effective flow. What is the safest immediate simulated response?

learnerSurfaces.locator: Suction transfer, best option
learnerSurfaces.excerpt: Reduce support temporarily, reassess filling and position, and address the cause first

learnerSurfaces.locator: Suction transfer, best option rationale (rewritten)
learnerSurfaces.excerpt: The supplied Impella CP instructions for use give this order for a suction alarm

learnerSurfaces.locator: Suction transfer, explanation (rewritten)
learnerSurfaces.excerpt: In this model a one- or two-level reduction leaves the suction pattern in place

items.learnerWording: Before: rationale “This limits ongoing suction while preserving a structured patient–position–device evaluation.”; explanation “The learner must make a real pump-level adjustment and identify the loading mechanism.” After: the IFU order, and what the model does after a reduction.
items.intendedTeachingPoint: Escalating through suction is unsafe; a reduction is a first step while the cause of underfilling is found and corrected.

sourceLocations.location: PDF p. 236 (printed 7.17), 'Suction with the Impella CP with SmartAssist Catheter'
sourceLocations.note: For a Suction or Impella Flow Reduced alarm: reduce the P-level by one or two; ensure adequate volume; check positioning with imaging and reposition slightly; evaluate RV function by invasive hemodynamics and/or echocardiography; once resolved, slowly resume the previous level. In AUTO mode the controller itself reduces speed to resolve suction.
For the right-sided pump: decrease the P-level as needed to resolve suction at P-7 to P-9; the displayed flow may be higher than actual.

sourceLocations.location: Model replay of the transfer setup (this batch)
sourceLocations.note: Reducing one or two levels keeps the suction alarm; four or more levels down clears it with a low-flow alarm; restoring filling clears both. The model has no AUTO mode and no position or imaging feedback.

sourceCheck.result: The best option matches the first step of the supplied CP instructions, which continue with volume, imaging and RV function. The previous rationale claimed the reduction limits suction, which the model does not show at one or two levels.

items.modelOutput: Setup (CP P-8, preload 55%): left 1.87, native 2.04, effective 3.91, MAP 61–63; suction and hemolysis-risk alarms. P-6: effective 3.57, MAP 58, suction persists plus low flow. P-5: 3.40, MAP 55, suction persists. P-4: 3.31, MAP 54, low-flow alarm only. P-3: 3.11; P-2: 2.89. P-8 with preload 85%: effective 5.71, MAP 89, no alarm. P-6 then preload 85%: 5.22, no alarm; back to P-8: 5.72, no alarm.
items.unresolvedDisagreement: In the model a one- or two-level reduction does not clear suction, while the instructions list it first and describe AUTO mode resolving suction by reducing speed. Whether the model's suction threshold is a fair teaching example is for review.
items.missingAndReassess: The model cannot show volume status, pump position on imaging or right ventricular function. Those are what to reassess before returning to the previous level; a lower alarm burden after a large reduction is not a resolved cause.
items.clinicalQuestion: Are the stated order and the model's response to a reduction an accurate teaching example? Should the transfer show restoring filling as the step that clears the pattern?
items.questionDisposition: mcs-impella-suction-transfer-1: keep as reinforcement (it contrasts escalation, a purge explanation and a structured reduction); rationale and explanation rewritten; still draft.
items.hold: The model's suction response to a reduction; wording of the new rationale and explanation.
items.changeInThisBatch: Best-option rationale and explanation rewritten to the IFU order and the replayed model. Options, key and required action unchanged.
